Class CausalClock

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalClock
public final class CausalClock extends Object
A vector clock over causal coordinates: a set of (topic, partition) → offset entries indexed by channel, the topic-partition, rather than by process (Fidge 1988; Mattern 1988). A Kafka partition is the stable, durable axis that a process identity is not.

One type plays both classical vector-clock roles, depending on where the instance sits:

  • VT(m), attached to a record: its causal dependencies, the positions a consumer must have observed before the record may be delivered.
  • VT(p), accumulated at a topology edge: a running frontier of everything this node has observed.

At an edge, hold a running instance as your VT(p): using(Properties) binds a resolver, observe(ConsumerRecord) folds in each record you consume, and stamp(ProducerRecord) attaches the result to each record you produce. Use builder(Properties) to assert a dependency you did not consume, and toBytes() / fromBytes(byte[]) to serialise. The serialised form is 5 + 28 × coordinates bytes and counts against Kafka's message.max.bytes, so watch a wide fan-in that depends on many topic-partitions.

  • Method Details

    • empty

      public static CausalClock empty()
      Returns an empty instance with no positions recorded and no resolver bound. To accumulate a clock from consumed records, prefer using(Properties), which binds a resolver so observe(ConsumerRecord) needs no per-call resolver argument.
      Returns:
      an empty CausalClock

    • using

      public static CausalClock using(Properties props)
      Returns an empty instance bound to a resolver over props, the start of a consumer-side frontier: bind the resolver once here, then observe(ConsumerRecord) each record you consume. The bound resolver flows through observe and merge(CausalClock) but is never serialised and never affects equality.
      Parameters:
      props - the Kafka client configuration to resolve topic UUIDs through; must not be null
      Returns:
      an empty CausalClock bound to a resolver over props

    • using

      public static CausalClock using(Map<String, org.apache.kafka.common.Uuid> topicIds)
      Returns an empty instance bound to a resolver over a fixed name→UUID map — the broker-free path for tests or callers that already hold the UUIDs. See using(Properties).
      Parameters:
      topicIds - the topic names mapped to their Kafka UUIDs; must not be null
      Returns:
      an empty CausalClock bound to a resolver over topicIds

    • merge

      public CausalClock merge(CausalClock other)
      Returns the causal union of this clock and other — the per-coordinate maximum offset (the vector-clock join). Use this to combine the clocks of several consumed records before stamping a fan-in record.
      Parameters:
      other - the clock to merge in; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new CausalClock dominating both inputs

    • observe

      public CausalClock observe(org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord<?,?> record)
      Folds a consumed record into this clock and returns the result: the union of this clock, the clock record carried, and, for a business record, record's own position (topic, partition, offset). Offsets take the per-coordinate maximum, so re-observing is safe. Requires a resolver, bound via using(Properties) or builder(Properties) or carried through a prior observe / merge.

      A null message (see isNullMessage(ConsumerRecord)) folds in only the completeness frontier it carries, never its own offset, since it delivers no business payload and gating on that offset would stall downstream on a record that carries nothing.

      Parameters:
      record - the consumed record to fold in; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new CausalClock extended with record's past and, for a business record, its own position
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no resolver is bound, or if record carries a malformed clock header
      IllegalArgumentException - if record's topic cannot be resolved to a UUID (business records only; a null message's topic is never resolved)

    • isNullMessage

      public static boolean isNullMessage(org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.ConsumerRecord<?,?> record)
      Returns true if record is a Parsley null message: a metadata record carrying a node's completeness frontier but no business payload. A plain Kafka client should still observe one, so its frontier advances across a service that emitted only null messages, but must not surface it as a business record. The usual loop is to observe every record and continue past those this flags.
      Parameters:
      record - the consumed record to test; must not be null
      Returns:
      true if the record carries the Parsley null-message marker header

    • stamp

      public <K,V> org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerRecord<K,V> stamp(org.apache.kafka.clients.producer.ProducerRecord<K,V> record)
      Returns a copy of record carrying this clock in its parsley-causal-clock header, ready to send through a plain Kafka producer. The input record is never mutated: a fresh header set is built (preserving every other header), and stamping is idempotent — any existing clock header is replaced, not duplicated.
      Type Parameters:
      K - the record key type
      V - the record value type
      Parameters:
      record - the record to stamp; must not be null
      Returns:
      a new ProducerRecord with the clock header attached
